title: Embed fastpath scheduler and kernel coexecution — p99 surgery
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Reduce embedding endpoint p99 latency for the common 1-8 token sequence workload without regressing throughput or retrieval/reranking quality. Scope covers: micro-batch shaping at ingress, a fastpath scheduler that bypasses heavyweight kernels for short sequences, coordinated kernel coexecution hints for the runtime, and rollout+monitoring.

Background: Production p99 for single-tenant embedding routes serving short sequences currently hovers ~520ms under bursty load; steady-state p50 ~42ms. We observe frequent tail amplification due to one or two long-running kernel invocations and suboptimal micro-batch packing during traffic spikes. Prior work on opportunistic coalescing improved throughput but sometimes increased jitter for high-priority traffic.

Acceptance criteria (must pass):
- Production p99 reduced to <=250ms on target endpoints (measured across two-week traffic slice with identical SLOs).
- No measurable degradation in embedding quality for reranking workflows: NDCG@10 drop <=0.3% and cosine-sim recall delta <=0.5% on the rerank evaluation set.
- Throughput (tokens/sec) no worse than -5% vs baseline under representative load.
- Rollout plan, automated canary, and rollback hooks implemented in Console.

Success metrics:
- p99 latency (edge -> response) target <=250ms, p95 <=120ms
- Embedding cost per 1M vectors reduced by >=15% (secondary metric)
- SLO violation rate <=0.1% during canary window

Technical approach (high level):
1) Fastpath scheduler: lightweight decision layer at ingress that identifies short-sequence embedding requests (<=8 tokens) and routes them to prewarmed fast workers using a small, optimized kernel path (fused GEMM+softmax where applicable). The scheduler also tags requests with a priority tag for coexecution hints.
2) Micro-batch shaping: adaptively shape micro-batches by inflight age and sequence-length histogram. Rather than fixed micro-batch size, we implement TTL-based micro-batch flush thresholds (age cap + occupancy cap) to bound tail amplification during spikes.
3) Kernel coexecution hints: extend kernel selection metadata so that the runtime can co-schedule short fastpath kernels on SMs that are not running long-attention kernels; add a 'coexec-safe' annotation for kernels to opt into softer preemption.
4) Quantization-aware tuning: experiment with 8-bit quantized kernels for the fastpath, but gate exposure behind offline eval to ensure rerank NDCG stays within threshold.
5) Observability and tooling: add a Console dashboard with per-route p50/p95/p99, micro-batch occupancy histogram, kernel-type latency breakdown, and per-request trace linking to PR/trace IDs.

Trade-offs and risks:
- Quantized fastpath may slightly change embedding geometry; must validate with rerank evals and holdback buckets.
- Preferring fastpath for short sequences may reduce unit GPU utilization; mitigate via autoscaling/growth policies and opportunistic backfill.
- Kernel coexecution hints add complexity to runtime scheduler and may interact with Dedicated capacity autoscaler — need careful canary.

Rollout plan:
- Local benchmarks + CI microbench harness (perf/latency/throughput) -> internal canary (5% traffic, 48h) -> regional canary (us-west-2 20%, 72h) -> global ramp to 100% with automated guardrails.

Rollback: automatic fallback to existing micro-batcher and kernel selection when SLOs degrade (console rollback trigger + manual revert PR).
